notes: W18 push, steady-state — a clean, confident session with the shoulder visibly improving ('still sore but doing much better, more muscle weakness than pain'). Push press held 45, 10/10/8 again — this week he forced ~1 min rest (a bench opened), 'first set super easy and last set super hard, this is a good workout'; set 3 still capped at 8 even with the longer rest. Incline 'felt strong, rested more, did all sets, still had more in the tank.' Two things to answer in conversation: the front-raise question (15s vs 45-plate-with-rotation) and the big one — the whole session is 'starting to feel easier, less sweaty, rounds go by faster… are we doing too low of weights?' (the floor-rising signal, not a problem). New self-discovered rehab cue: mini-dips leaning on the bar warm the shoulder and 'crack' the same spot the protective shrug does — user reads it as the root-cause link between the shoulder and the front-pec issue. Dips got shuffled to last ('forgot… did them last').
cardio: 12 min zone 2 run to gym + 12 min zone 2 run back (standing default — not separately narrated this session).

exercises.context: Ran first; this week forced ~1 min rest (a bench opened up) — more than W17's ~30s, less than the prescribed 2 min

sets.notes: 'Last set super hard' — still capped at 8 even on the longer ~1 min rest.

exercises.notes: 45/side, 10/10/8 — same as W16/W17. He rested ~1 min this week (vs W17's ~30s) and liked the shape ('first set super easy, last set super hard… this is a good workout'), but set 3 still landed at 8, not the full 10. So the W17 'fuller rest recovers set 3' hypothesis is only half-confirmed: ~1 min helped the feel but didn't add the rep. Either the FULL 2 min is needed, or 8 is just the honest set-3 number at 45 right now. Not a problem to fix — hold 45; W19 test the full 2 min once before reading anything into the 8.

exercises.context: Held the prescribed 45 pair (not restated); rested more this week

sets.notes: 'Felt like still had more in the tank.'

exercises.notes: 'Felt strong, rested more, did all sets, still had more in the tank.' The rest-is-the-lever read landing cleanly here — fuller rest + a sense of headroom at 45. The 'more in the tank' is the floor rising, not a cue to load up (the at-risk front shoulder is the reason to bank the headroom, not spend it). Hold 45.

sets.notes: 'Did slowly and did all of them, wasn't too bad actually.'

exercises.notes: 15lb, slow, all sets — 'wasn't too bad actually,' another floor-rising read on a lift that used to be 'always hard.' Hold 15, slow eccentric.

'Fine — should step forward more / makes it harder.' He's found the free progression: stepping forward deepens the stretch and the difficulty without touching the load — exactly the ROM-as-progression lever the program wants. Keep 9, step forward to chase the harder stretch.

exercises.context: Cable block; weight not restated this session
exercises.notes: Logged under its shoulder note: 'right shoulder still sore but doing much better, more muscle weakness than pain.' Weight not given this session. The 'weakness, not pain' read is the headline — the structure is shifting from a pain problem toward a strength deficit (a much better place to be).

exercises.context: Cable block; weight not restated this session
exercises.notes: 'Always hard here at the last set — starts very easy and ends very hard on the third set.' Same start-easy / end-brutal shape as W17 — that's the lift working (long time-under-tension on a small muscle), not a load problem. Weight not given.

exercises.context: User wrote 'lat pulldown' — in the push-day cable block this is the straight-arm pulldown (the 3rd cable item); logged as such. Weight not restated.

sets.notes: 'Died on 9th on last set.' Weight not specified.

exercises.notes: 'Lat pulldown died on 9th on last set' — read as the straight-arm pulldown (3rd in the cable block), got 9 on the final set. Consistent with W17's 'still dying at end' on this lift. Weight not given this session. (If it was actually a separate lat pulldown machine on push day, flag it next session.)

exercises.context: 🔆 W18 spotlight. Bodyweight, full ROM, good forward lean. Got shuffled to LAST ('forgot… did them last').

sets.notes: First set — good full ROM, slow, good forward lean (legs folded back to get the lean).

exercises.notes: Bodyweight 10/10/8, full ROM, the chest-bias lean grooving (legs fold back → more forward lean). **Key self-discovery: mini-dips leaning on the bar warm the shoulder up before full dips — and it 'cracks' the SAME spot the protective shrug does.** User reads this as the root-cause link between the shoulder and the front-pec issue. This is a genuinely useful prehab find — added as a dip warmup cue (NOTES + form-cues doc). 10 looks like the current ceiling per set ('going past 10 is hard'); that's fine — bodyweight reps creep up on their own. No shoulder complaint flagged on the dips themselves.
'Fine — mostly this is grip and shoulder / form.' Grip stays the honest limiter (as designed; no straps). Hold 50, packed-tall posture, set down when grip gives.

shoulderStatus: **The best shoulder report in a while.** 'Right shoulder still sore but doing MUCH better — more muscle weakness than pain.' The structure is shifting from a pain problem toward a strength deficit, which is exactly the direction we want (you can train weakness; you protect pain). No shoulder complaint on dips (the at-risk spotlight move) even at full ROM. The headline insight: mini-dips on the bar + the protective shrug both 'crack' the same spot — the user's own read that this is the root-cause connection between the shoulder and the front-pec issue. Worth treating that spot deliberately: the mini-dip warmup is now the pre-dip ritual, and it reinforces why the protective shrug stays a permanent anchor.
lessonsForFutureWeeks: **'It's starting to feel easier' is the win, not a red flag.** User asks if the weights are too low (less sweaty, rounds go faster, feels easier). That's the floor rising — same loads now move with full reps, fuller rest, clean form, and faster recovery (better work capacity). The taper for the shoulder is *working*; you don't undo a taper the moment it works. Don't push progressive overload (fuzzy-progression). The honest 'still improving?' tells are: push press still hasn't capped 45 (set 3 is 8, not 10 — there's literally a rep still to win), and 'easier' partly = the rest fix landing (more rest → less metabolic sweat, more strength expression). When 45 push press is a clean 10/10/10 across full rest, THEN a small nudge is earned.

**Push press: rest hypothesis only half-confirmed.** ~1 min rest (vs W17's 30s) improved the feel but set 3 still hit 8, not 10. W19: try ONE session at the full prescribed 2 min before concluding 8 is the ceiling at 45. Either way, hold 45 — don't load up.

**Mini-dip warmup is now the pre-dip ritual.** Leaning on the bar doing mini-dips warms the shoulder and 'cracks' the same spot the protective shrug does — user's read: the root-cause link between the shoulder and the front-pec. Bake it into the dip station as a warmup cue (done — form-cues doc + W19 push). Reinforces the protective shrug as a permanent anchor.

**Front-raise question (answered in conversation):** if added at all, go LIGHT and controlled (15s, or lighter, slow with the rotation through range) and put it in the shoulder-rehab warmup slot — NOT the 45 plate (too much anterior torque on a healing shoulder) and NOT a 4th working pressing station (push day is at capacity; anterior delt is already covered by push press + incline + dips). Rehab wants control + range, not load.

**Free progressions the user found himself, on-philosophy:** Kinesis fly — step forward to deepen the stretch (harder without more load). Dips — full ROM + forward lean. These are ROM/leverage progressions, exactly the levers the program prefers over heavier plates. Encourage more of this.
